newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand weakened 1.5 cents on Monday to its lowest level in five months as local importers and banks positioned themselves ahead of Tuesday's foreign exchange control relaxation.

At 1400 GMT, it was quoted at 4.5280/5310 against the dollar from 4.5145/5175 late on Friday after touching a day's weakest level of 4.5295 bid -- its lowest since February 5 when it touched 4.5330 bid.
"Once again we've seen pressure on the rand ahead of tomorrow. Importers have been covering a bit...and we've seen a bit of buying from the local banks as well," a trader said.
On Tuesday, South African individuals will be allowed to invest 200,000 rand offshore or hold that amount in foreign exchange in a local bank account.

The markets had been nervous of the move, fearing a wholesale exodus of capital from the country, but their concerns have been soothed by the Reserve Bank's buildup of reserves and credit lines of some 38 billion rand which it has said it can access to smooth possible market volatility.
Dealers said the diminishing unease about the move was reflected in the rand.
"If you look at the rand at 4.53 it is not bad at all. It has performed very well considering the exchange control move," a trader said.
On Tuesday, dealers said the rand was expected to weaken further although mainly on sentiment and not on any outflow of dollars.

"It is going to be a normal day's trade tomorrow. The only thing that changes is that people can start applying to take money out which is not going to be aproved immediately so it doesn't have an immediate effect," a trader said.
"The only effect is sentiment."
Dealers said that with the prospect of a weaker rand, exporters were content to hold on to their dollars for now.
"We are still seeing demand for dollars and it is a foregone conclusion that the rand weakens.
"It is not going to be dramatic and it's not necessarily going to be a rush so people are happier buying and covering on the import side and the exporters are waiting for better levels."
One trader said he expected a 4.5250 to 4.5350 range on Tuesday, while another said the rand could head towards 4.55 where offshore players were likely to sell dollars.
The rand also dropped to a fresh low against sterling, hitting 7.5602 at one point -- its weakest since January 22, this year -- before recovering to 7.5379/5508 from 7.5008/5094 on Friday.
Against the mark it was last trading at 0.3838/3843 marks from 0.3843/3848 marks previously and at 25.1996/2494 yen from 25.3437/3798 yen before.
On the bond market, yields edged higher in what traders said was a market that appeared technically overbought.
The R150 was last yielding 14.36 percent from 14.30 percent from Friday.
Dealers said trade on the day had been characterised by good foreign and local institutional demand, but that after its recent downrun, the market appeared in need of a slight correction.

"Technically it is looking a bit overbought and I would say we should be looking at 14.44 (percent) where we can flush out a few of the longs, let the guys take some profits and head down again," one trader said.
Dealers said concern about July 1, in the bond market was relatively muted and players were focussing their attention on the gold and foreign exchange reserves which are due out on Tuesday.
Economists expect reserves to show a three billion rand increase in June to 24.68 billion rand from 21.8 billion rand in May.
Money market rates held steady in early trade. Three-month NCDs were quoted at 15.85 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was at between 15.40 and 15.25 percent.
The Reserve Bank quoted the money market shortage at 5.376 billion rand on Saturday from 5.378 billion rand on Friday.
Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net sellers of 267.89 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Friday after buying 39.04 million rand's worth on Thursday.
Nominal cumulative volumes on the bond market on Friday were 9.48 billion rand from 44.75 billion rand on Thursday -- settlement day.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
